overall: The AG found the BRA did not violate the Open Meeting Law: notice was timely posted and listed a detailed topic, opening and closing required no specific procedure, and non-OML allegations were declined.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the BRA gave improper notice of its July 12, 2012 meeting, which had 23 listed topics including a Washington Street project.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the BRA properly posted its meeting notice and did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the BRA failed to properly open and close the July 12, 2012 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Additionally, the Open Meeting Law does not require that public bodies follow any specific procedure to open or close a meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint raised non-OML matters: abutter notice, site plan availability, a project address, neighborhood council notice, land ownership, and time stamping of records.
allegations.key_passage: Because these allegations, even if true, would not constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law, we decline to review them.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
